archetypes.name: Short (Hertzian) dipole
archetypes.summary: Electrically short centre-fed dipole with an assumed triangular current distribution.

parameters.name: electrical length
parameters.description: total length as a fraction of the free-space wavelength

synthesis.notes: tip-to-tip length

analysis.notes: Rr = 20*pi^2*(L/lambda)^2 for the triangular current distribution a real short dipole carries (Balanis 4-37). This is the practical value.

Rr = 80*pi^2*(L/lambda)^2, the uniform-current infinitesimal dipole (Balanis 4-19). Four times the triangular value, because Rr scales with the square of the effective length (L/2 triangular, L uniform). Reached in practice only by capacitive top loading - see top_loaded_monopole.
exact for sin^2 theta
L/2 for the triangular distribution; L for a uniform current
exact for the sin^2 pattern

validity: L < 0.1*lambda, beyond which the current is no longer approximately linear
thin wire, radius << L
Rr excludes ohmic and ground loss; a short dipole's efficiency is usually loss-dominated

known_cases.source: Rr = 20*pi^2*(0.01)^2 = 0.019739 ohm triangular, 80*pi^2*(0.01)^2 = 0.078957 ohm uniform; D = 1.5 = 1.761 dBi. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., eqs. 4-19 and 4-37
quadratic scaling check: 25x the 0.01 case. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 (eqs. 4-19, 4-26)

archetypes.name: Half-wave dipole
archetypes.summary: The canonical centre-fed dipole of exactly half a wavelength; the reference antenna for dBd.

parameters.name: wire radius
parameters.description: conductor radius; only the reactance depends on it

synthesis.notes: exactly lambda/2; see resonant_dipole for the length that actually resonates
log10(lambda/aw), the same thickness variable resonant_dipole uses

analysis.notes: exact Balanis 4-70; 73.08 ohm with eta0 = 376.73 (textbooks quoting 73.13 use 120*pi). This is the INDUCED-EMF radiation resistance of an ASSUMED sinusoidal current on a vanishingly thin wire, and it is independent of wire radius by construction. It is the canonical reference value and stays exactly that. It is NOT what a real wire presents at its terminals - see input_resistance_driving_point_ohm.
exact Balanis 4-79; +42.5 ohm at exactly lambda/2, which is why real dipoles are cut short. Induced-EMF, like the resistance beside it.

The induced-EMF pair 73.08 + j42.52 - the number every textbook quotes and the reference dBd rests on. A delta-gap-fed wire of finite radius presents something else, and the difference grows with the wire: see the driving_point metrics.

numerically integrated for the sinusoidal current; see otahub.core.pattern.finite_dipole(0.5). The definitional value dBd is measured against, and kept as such. The solved current is slightly fatter near the ends and gives 1.645 to 1.657 - 0.25 to 1.0% higher, growing with the wire.
numerically integrated
l_e = lambda/pi for a half-wave dipole

What a real wire presents at exactly half a wavelength: 78.0 ohm on 1e-5 lambda wire rising to 94.7 on 2.7e-3 - 7% to 30% above the canonical 73.08, because the real current is fatter than a sinusoid near the ends. It tends to 73.08 only as the wire vanishes, and slowly, logarithmically. Worst fit error 0.25%. Method of moments (otahub/num/mom.py), delta-gap fed. The INDUCED-EMF closed forms this archetype also carries are exact for an ASSUMED sinusoidal current on a vanishingly thin wire; they are a different quantity from what a real wire presents at its terminals, which is what this is. The difference is not mesh error: an independent Hallen solve agrees with the MoM, and feeding the MoM the sinusoidal current instead reproduces the induced-EMF value to 0.3%.
44.3 to 46.6 ohm over the fitted range, against the canonical 42.52. Worst fit error 0.34%.

validity: free space, no ground plane or nearby structure
thin wire: the reactance formula assumes aw << L
at exactly lambda/2 the antenna is NOT resonant (X = +42.5 ohm)

the driving-point metrics cover aw from 1e-5 to 2.7e-3 wavelengths; beyond that the resistance turns up sharply (110 ohm at 5e-3) where thin-wire theory itself starts to strain, so it is not extrapolated

known_cases.source: Balanis: Rr = 73.13 ohm, X = +42.5 ohm, D = 1.643 (2.15 dBi) at L = lambda/2
lambda/2 at 2.4 GHz = 62.44 mm

Both at once, deliberately: the canonical induced-EMF 73.08 ohm, which does not depend on the wire, beside the driving-point resistance of a real aw = 0.0001 lambda wire from the method of moments, which does. The two differ by 10% here, and an independent Hallen solve sides with the MoM.

Both at once, deliberately: the canonical induced-EMF 73.08 ohm, which does not depend on the wire, beside the driving-point resistance of a real aw = 0.001 lambda wire from the method of moments, which does. The two differ by 18% here, and an independent Hallen solve sides with the MoM.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 (eqs. 4-70, 4-79)

archetypes.name: Resonant dipole (thickness corrected)
archetypes.summary: A dipole shortened from lambda/2 so that its input reactance is zero at f0.

synthesis.notes: t = log10(lambda/aw)

Quadratic fit to the exact zero of Balanis 4-79, computed over a/lambda = 1e-5..1e-2 (L/d = 50 to 50000). Max error 0.42% of a wavelength across that range. Outside it, solve X(L) = 0 directly. Checked against an open tube with a finite gap (otahub.num.bor, its rims resolved) out to 0.025 wavelengths: inside the spread the feed itself causes, +-0.3% at 0.005 to +-3% at 0.025, from 0.0075 on; at 0.005 and below it sits 0.2-0.35% above the tube's longest resonance. Thin-wire theory has no rim: at a = 0.002 the converged exact-kernel thin-wire MoM resonates at 0.4712, the rim-resolved tube at 0.4706 and the law at 0.4720 - all inside the fit's own 0.42%.

analysis.notes: INDUCED-EMF radiation resistance (Balanis 4-70) for an assumed sinusoidal current at this length: 58.7 to 67.1 ohm. This spec used to present it as what the antenna presents - '55-68 ohm across practical thicknesses' - and it is not. The driving-point resistance is input_resistance_ohm, and it is 6 to 28% higher, worst on thick wire. Kept because it is the textbook quantity, now named for what it is.

What a real wire presents at its terminals at this length: 71.9 to 75.6 ohm, and remarkably flat - within 2 ohm of 72.5 from aw = 1e-5 to 2.7e-3 wavelengths, turning up only for the fattest conductors. The folk figure 'a resonant dipole is about 72 ohm' is right; the closed form this spec used to quote in its place was 6 to 22% low, worst on thick wire. Worst fit error 0.46%. Method of moments (otahub/num/mom.py), delta-gap fed. The INDUCED-EMF closed forms this archetype also carries are exact for an ASSUMED sinusoidal current on a vanishingly thin wire; they are a different quantity from what a real wire presents at its terminals, which is what this is. The difference is not mesh error: an independent Hallen solve agrees with the MoM, and feeding the MoM the sinusoidal current instead reproduces the induced-EMF value to 0.3%.

The INDUCED-EMF reactance, which is zero at this length by construction of the length fit. A real wire at the same length is not quite resonant: the solver finds -3.1 to +6.2 ohm of residual reactance, because the length was tuned to the closed form rather than to the wire. Small, but 'zero by construction' was a statement about the model, not the antenna. Not fitted: a quantity that crosses zero has no meaningful relative error.

Resistive-only estimate against 50 ohm, now from the DRIVING-POINT resistance. It used the induced-EMF value, which put a thin resonant dipole at about 1.26:1 in 50 ohm when a real one sits nearer 1.45:1 - optimistic in the one number a builder is most likely to check first.

Integrated from the solved current at this length: 1.635 to 1.639, a whisker below the half-wave 1.6409 this spec used to borrow. Its own note was right that the shortening barely changes the pattern; it just used the wrong antenna's number to say so. Worst fit error 0.020%.

Computed: the VSWR = 2 window about the wire's own resonance, referenced to its own resonant resistance. 5.7% on 1e-5 lambda wire to 17.4% on 5e-3 - a factor of three across the gauges, which is the quantitative form of 'fat dipoles are broadband'. Cross-checked against the Yaghjian-Best Q. Worst fit error 1.01%.
From |dZ/dw| at resonance: 12.4 on the thinnest wire down to 4.1 on the fattest. Worst fit error 0.63%.

validity: 1e-5 < aw/lambda < 1e-2; outside this the length fit is untested
thin-wire theory: no insulation, no end capacitance from hardware
free space; height above ground shifts resonance by more than this correction

input_resistance_ohm, bandwidth, Q and directivity are full-wave values for a delta-gap-fed wire in free space; radiation_resistance_ohm and input_reactance_ohm are the induced-EMF closed forms and describe an assumed sinusoidal current, not the wire
the fits cover aw from 1e-5 to 5e-3 wavelengths

past aw of about 0.005 wavelengths the resonance is a property of the feed as well as the wire. Solved as an open tube with a finite gap (otahub.num.bor, rims resolved), gaps from a/2 to 4a spread the resonant length by +-0.3% at aw = 0.005, +-0.9% at 0.01 and +-2-4% at 0.015-0.025 wavelengths, and the resistance over 72-74, 73-78 and 74-97 ohm. The length law stays inside that spread from aw = 0.0075 on and sits 0.2-0.35% above it at 0.005 and below (the tube's rim, which thin-wire theory does not have); the resistance law, fitted to delta-gap solutions, sits at its small-gap end. At 0.025 wavelengths a gap of a/2 leaves the dipole with no resonance at all

known_cases.source: exact zero of Balanis 4-79 at a/lambda = 1e-4 is L = 0.48463 lambda Reactance is checked with an absolute tolerance of 6 ohm: the length fit carries 0.42% error, which maps to a few ohm of residual reactance against a 66 ohm radiation resistance (VSWR < 1.1).
exact zero at a/lambda = 1e-3 is L = 0.47751 lambda
exact zero at a/lambda = 1e-2 is L = 0.45738 lambda, Rr = 55.74 ohm

Method of moments at aw = 0.0001 lambda on the spec's own length: the nearest solved point, aw = 0.00012, gives R = 73.09 ohm against the induced-EMF closed form's lower figure, a 7.75% VSWR = 2 window and Q = 9.16. The closed form reproduces itself exactly when the MoM is handed the sinusoidal current, which is how the gap was traced to the current shape rather than to the mesh.

Method of moments at aw = 0.001 lambda on the spec's own length: the nearest solved point, aw = 0.000775, gives R = 72.71 ohm against the induced-EMF closed form's lower figure, a 10.57% VSWR = 2 window and Q = 6.74. The closed form reproduces itself exactly when the MoM is handed the sinusoidal current, which is how the gap was traced to the current shape rather than to the mesh.

Method of moments at aw = 0.003 lambda on the spec's own length: the nearest solved point, aw = 0.00269, gives R = 73.56 ohm against the induced-EMF closed form's lower figure, a 14.11% VSWR = 2 window and Q = 5.08. The closed form reproduces itself exactly when the MoM is handed the sinusoidal current, which is how the gap was traced to the current shape rather than to the mesh.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 (eq. 4-79)

archetypes.name: Quarter-wave monopole over a ground plane
archetypes.summary: Half a dipole over an infinite perfect ground plane; image theory doubles the directivity.

synthesis.notes: the equivalent dipole formed with the image
log10(lambda/aw), the same thickness variable resonant_dipole uses

analysis.notes: Induced-EMF: half the half-wave dipole's 73.08 - same radiated power into half the space - for an ASSUMED sinusoidal current on a vanishing wire; 36.54 ohm. What a real wire presents at its base is input_resistance_driving_point_ohm.
+21.26 ohm at exactly lambda/4
The induced-EMF pair, 36.54 + j21.26: the textbook figure. A delta-gap-fed wire of finite radius presents the driving-point pair.
twice the dipole: radiation confined to the upper hemisphere
5.16 dBi
elevation half-power beamwidth measured from the horizon upward

What a real wire presents at its base at exactly a quarter wave over a perfect ground plane: by image theory exactly half the driving-point resistance of the half-wave dipole of the same wire (half_wave_dipole's method-of-moments fit), 39.0 ohm on 1e-5 lambda wire rising to 47.4 on 2.7e-3 - not the induced-EMF 36.54 beside it, which assumes a sinusoidal current on a vanishing wire. The monopole of 2h solved directly as a dipole by the method of moments and by Hallen's equation, halved, agrees within 0.4%.
Half the dipole's driving-point reactance: 22.2 to 23.3 ohm over the fitted range, against the induced-EMF 21.26.

validity: infinite, perfectly conducting ground plane
a finite ground plane raises Rin and tilts the pattern upward; below about 0.25*lambda radius the effect is severe
real earth is lossy: ground loss often exceeds radiation resistance at HF
the driving-point metrics cover aw from 1e-5 to 2.7e-3 wavelengths, as half_wave_dipole's do

known_cases.source: Half the half-wave dipole impedance: 36.5 + j21.25 ohm; D = 5.15 dBi. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4

A quarter-wave monopole of radius 1e-04 lambda over perfect ground is, by image theory, half a half-wave dipole: that dipole solved directly (not the fit) by the method of moments, exact kernel, 120 segments, 80.330+45.321j ohm, and by Hallen's equation 80.342+45.356j; halved, 40.165+22.661j ohm at the base - against the induced-EMF 36.54 + j21.26, which does not depend on the wire.

A quarter-wave monopole of radius 1e-03 lambda over perfect ground is, by image theory, half a half-wave dipole: that dipole solved directly (not the fit) by the method of moments, exact kernel, 120 segments, 86.534+46.613j ohm, and by Hallen's equation 86.810+46.966j; halved, 43.267+23.306j ohm at the base - against the induced-EMF 36.54 + j21.26, which does not depend on the wire.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 Ch. 4.7 (image theory)

archetypes.name: Folded dipole
archetypes.summary: Two parallel conductors shorted at the ends: four times a dipole's resonant resistance, about 1.6 times its bandwidth, and a few percent shorter than a plain dipole at resonance.

synthesis.notes: Nominal starting length. resonant_length_m is what actually resonates, and it is 1.3 to 6.6% shorter - the two conductors and the end shorts load the structure.
typical practical spacing, 0.01-0.05 lambda; must stay << lambda for the transmission-line mode to be non-radiating
Omega on the NOMINAL length, so nothing here is circular.

Length at which the reactance crosses zero: 0.449 to 0.474 lambda over the spacings and wire gauges here, against the flat 0.48 this spec synthesises. Wider spacing shortens it markedly - 0.474 at d = 0.005 lambda down to 0.450 at 0.04. Worst fit error 0.09%. Method of moments (otahub/num/mom.py), whose folded-dipole geometry is one of the six cases licensing the solver. Bandwidth is computed twice by routes sharing no algebra - directly, by finding where VSWR crosses 2 either side of resonance, and through the antenna Q of Yaghjian and Best, Q = (w0/2R0)|dZ/dw| - and they agree to 2.0% at worst, widening with bandwidth exactly as the narrowband Q approximation should.

analysis.notes: Verified, with a caveat about what it means. Comparing each structure AT ITS OWN RESONANCE the ratio is 3.949 to 4.021 across every spacing and gauge tested - the classic 4:1 is a law, not a coincidence. Comparing at the SAME FREQUENCY it is nothing of the kind: it runs from 2.2 to 4.9 across a 20% span of length, because the transmission-line mode does not scale with the radiating one. Only N = 2 was solved; higher N keeps the classical N^2.

284 to 290 ohm at resonance for the two-conductor case, against the 292.3 this spec computed as 4 x 73.079. The 1 to 3% overshoot is the induced-EMF 73.079 standing in for a real dipole's 72 ohm resonant resistance. Still the classic 300 ohm twin-lead match. Worst fit error 0.16%. Method of moments (otahub/num/mom.py), whose folded-dipole geometry is one of the six cases licensing the solver. Bandwidth is computed twice by routes sharing no algebra - directly, by finding where VSWR crosses 2 either side of resonance, and through the antenna Q of Yaghjian and Best, Q = (w0/2R0)|dZ/dw| - and they agree to 2.0% at worst, widening with bandwidth exactly as the narrowband Q approximation should.

COMPUTED, not indicative: the VSWR = 2 window about resonance, referenced to the antenna's own resonant resistance. 10.7% to 18.7% over the geometries here, against the flat 0.10 this spec asserted. And the folded dipole is NOT 'roughly twice' a plain dipole's bandwidth - measured against a plain dipole of the same wire gauge it is 1.36 to 1.72 times, never 2. Worst fit error 0.95%. Method of moments (otahub/num/mom.py), whose folded-dipole geometry is one of the six cases licensing the solver. Bandwidth is computed twice by routes sharing no algebra - directly, by finding where VSWR crosses 2 either side of resonance, and through the antenna Q of Yaghjian and Best, Q = (w0/2R0)|dZ/dw| - and they agree to 2.0% at worst, widening with bandwidth exactly as the narrowband Q approximation should.

The pattern is NOT quite 'indistinguishable from a plain dipole', as this spec used to say. It runs 1.1% up on the closest spacing and thinnest wire and 7.0% up on the widest and thickest - the two conductors are a short end-fire pair, and the gain grows with their separation. Small, 0.05 to 0.29 dB, but systematic rather than noise. Worst fit error 0.04%. Method of moments (otahub/num/mom.py), whose folded-dipole geometry is one of the six cases licensing the solver. Bandwidth is computed twice by routes sharing no algebra - directly, by finding where VSWR crosses 2 either side of resonance, and through the antenna Q of Yaghjian and Best, Q = (w0/2R0)|dZ/dw| - and they agree to 2.0% at worst, widening with bandwidth exactly as the narrowband Q approximation should.

validity: the fits cover conductor spacing 0.005 to 0.04 lambda and wire radius 1e-4 to 1e-3 lambda, with spacing at least six wire radii
N = 2 is the only case solved; the N^2 step-up for more conductors is classical and is not verified here
equal-diameter conductors. Unequal diameters divide the current unevenly and the step-up becomes (1 + alpha)^2 with alpha the division factor, which this spec does not model
free space, lossless, delta-gap feed, reduced thin-wire kernel
bandwidth is referenced to the antenna's OWN resonant resistance, so it is the best case: feeding it from 300 ohm line adds its own mismatch
the 4:1 step-up holds between structures AT RESONANCE; at a fixed frequency off resonance it is not 4 and not even constant

known_cases.source: Method of moments at d = 0.02 lambda, wire radius 0.0001 lambda: the reactance crosses zero at 0.46294 lambda with R = 286.06 ohm, which is 3.973 times a plain dipole's resonant resistance. The VSWR = 2 window is 12.18% wide, confirmed to 0.9% by the independent Q = (w0/2R0)|dZ/dw| route, against 7.56% for a plain dipole of the same gauge - a factor of 1.611, not the 'roughly twice' this spec claimed. Directivity 1.67111 against the plain dipole's 1.62307.

Method of moments at d = 0.01 lambda, wire radius 0.0003 lambda: the reactance crosses zero at 0.46717 lambda with R = 286.00 ohm, which is 3.975 times a plain dipole's resonant resistance. The VSWR = 2 window is 12.99% wide, confirmed to 1.0% by the independent Q = (w0/2R0)|dZ/dw| route, against 8.91% for a plain dipole of the same gauge - a factor of 1.457, not the 'roughly twice' this spec claimed. Directivity 1.66440 against the plain dipole's 1.62702.

Method of moments at d = 0.04 lambda, wire radius 0.001 lambda: the reactance crosses zero at 0.44848 lambda with R = 289.64 ohm, which is 4.021 times a plain dipole's resonant resistance. The VSWR = 2 window is 18.73% wide, confirmed to 2.0% by the independent Q = (w0/2R0)|dZ/dw| route, against 11.11% for a plain dipole of the same gauge - a factor of 1.686, not the 'roughly twice' this spec claimed. Directivity 1.73124 against the plain dipole's 1.61794.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 Ch. 9.5
Resonant length, resistance, directivity and VSWR bandwidth derived here by method of moments, with bandwidth cross-checked against the Yaghjian-Best antenna Q

archetypes.name: Biconical antenna
archetypes.summary: Two opposed cones; a travelling-wave structure whose impedance is set by the cone angle.

parameters.name: cone half angle
parameters.description: half angle measured from the axis; 30 deg = 0.5236 rad

parameters.name: spacing between the two cone tops
slant length at f0, in wavelengths

synthesis.notes: SOLVED, tabulated: the slant at which VSWR against the cone's own characteristic impedance first falls to 2 and stays there - the lowest frequency of a bicone fed from a line matched to it - from otahub.num.bor, extrapolated from two meshes. 0.223-0.288 wavelengths from 10 to 55 degrees, so the quarter-wave rule is right to 15% there; 0.332 at 65 degrees and 0.365 at 5, where it is not.
slant length of each cone, from the ideal apex
The feed: each cone truncated at 2% of its base diameter, as the solved model is.
Spacing between the two top faces - twice the conical monopole's 0.3 x top diameter, its image included.

analysis.notes: Zc = (eta0/pi) ln cot(theta_h/2) with theta_h the HALF angle, exact for the infinite biconical. This spec used cot(theta_h/4) - the same formula written for the FULL cone angle, as Kraus gives it - while documenting theta_h as the half angle, so every figure was the impedance of a cone half as wide: 243 ohm for a 30 degree cone that presents 158, and 188 for the classic 47 degree cone that presents 100. Two cross-consistency tests had been written with doubled angles to make this spec agree with its half-angle siblings, instead of catching the difference.

SOLVED, tabulated: peak directivity at f0, where the slant is k_slant. 1.558 at 30 degrees. The wire-cage fit this replaces was evaluated at a quarter-wave slant and ran 0.7-2.8% above the solid cone there; the rest of the difference is the cutoff moving. A narrow cone is a fat dipole and exceeds 1.64; a wide one falls well below, and at 65 degrees its beam has lifted 30 degrees off the horizon at f0.

SOLVED, tabulated: continuous band with VSWR under 2 against the characteristic impedance; 10 means it ran past a decade. It does from 10 to 65 degrees - the indicative decade was right, matched to Zc. At 5 degrees the VSWR pops back over 2 just above the cutoff (1.26:1), though it is under 2 again from twice f0.
SOLVED, tabulated: the highest VSWR against Zc between 2 f0 and 10 f0. 1.66 at 30 degrees.

validity: characteristic impedance is exact only for an infinite structure; the tables are for the finite cones solved
theta_h is the HALF angle from the axis, between 5 and 65 degrees
VSWR is against the cone's own characteristic impedance - a matched feed line; against any other reference the band differs
solid cones truncated at the stated feed (top 2% of the base diameter); a very different feed moves the band edges

known_cases.source: Body-of-revolution solve, 30 degrees: VSWR against Zc = 158 ohm falls to 2 at a slant of 0.2247 wavelengths, 67.36 mm at 1 GHz - 10% shorter than the quarter wave this spec used.
(eta0/pi) ln cot(15 deg) = 157.93 ohm, and the solved directivity at f0, 1.5581.
A narrow cone, 10 degrees: 292.15 ohm, and directivity 1.7517 at its cutoff slant of 0.2879 wavelengths - more than a half-wave dipole.
47 degrees, the 100 ohm bicone: directivity 1.4367 at f0.
30 degrees, matched to Zc: VSWR under 2 past a decade, worst 1.657 between 2 and 10 f0.
5 degrees: the band under VSWR 2 breaks off at 1.26 f0 before settling below 2 again.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 Ch. 10.3 (eq. 10-20)
Directivity solved here by method of moments on a wire cage; angle convention corrected to the half angle the parameter always documented
Cutoff, bandwidth and directivity solved here as a body of revolution (otahub.num.bor)

mom_directivity_across_band.source: Method of moments, 16-wire cages, free space

archetypes.name: Centre-fed dipole of arbitrary length
archetypes.summary: Sinusoidal-current dipole from 0.05 to 1.2 lambda, solved exactly in Si/Ci rather than by interpolation.

parameters.name: electrical length
parameters.description: tip-to-tip length as a fraction of the free-space wavelength

synthesis.notes: tip-to-tip

analysis.notes: Balanis 4-70, referred to the current maximum. Verified against direct numerical integration of the pattern at 0.1, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 and 1.25 lambda.

Referred to the FEED current, which for L != lambda/2 differs from the current maximum by sin(kL/2). The two coincide only at the half-wave point. Diverges as L approaches lambda, where the idealised sinusoid puts a current null at the feed; a real full-wave dipole shows a few kilohms, not infinity.
Balanis 4-79, referred to the current maximum - the companion of radiation_resistance_current_max_ohm.

Referred to the FEED. Balanis 4-79 is referred to the current MAXIMUM of the assumed sinusoid; for any length but lambda/2 that point is not the feed, and the feed-point value is the current-maximum one divided by sin^2(kL/2) - the same referral this catalogue already applied to the resistance. This spec carried the current-maximum value under this name while its resistance, one line up, was already referred to the feed - so its R and X described different points on the same antenna. At a quarter wavelength the error was a factor of two, at a tenth of a wavelength a factor of ten. Diverges near L = lambda exactly as the resistance does, for the same reason.
|F| at theta = 90 deg. Broadside remains the pattern maximum up to about 1.2 lambda, confirmed by scanning |F(theta)| on a 200k-point grid.
D = eta*|F|^2/(pi*Rm), exact for L <= 1.2 lambda. Reproduces 1.5010 at 0.1 lambda, 1.6409 at 0.5 and 2.4110 at 1.0 - the textbook full-wave dipole value.
dBd: how much this length buys over a half-wave dipole

validity: 0.05 < L/lambda < 1.2; above ~1.25 lambda the main beam splits and broadside is no longer the maximum
assumed sinusoidal current, which is the standard thin-wire idealisation
input resistance is unusable within a few percent of L = lambda, where the model puts a current null at the feed
no ground plane, no loss

known_cases.source: The half-wave dipole: 73.08 ohm and D = 1.641. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.6
Full-wave dipole: Rr = 199 ohm referred to the current maximum, D = 2.41. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Table 4.1 / Fig. 4.13
Quarter-wave dipole, independently reproduced by numerical integration of the sinusoidal-current pattern. The factor-of-two gap between the two resistances is the sin^2(kL/2) referral.

Balanis 4-79 at L = 0.1 lambda, aw = 1e-4 lambda: -183.37 ohm at the current maximum, -1920.24 ohm at the feed after dividing by sin^2(kL/2) = 0.09549. The method of moments gives -1857.38 ohm at the feed, within 3.4% of the referred value and nowhere near the unreferred one.

Balanis 4-79 at L = 0.25 lambda, aw = 1e-4 lambda: -361.40 ohm at the current maximum, -722.80 ohm at the feed after dividing by sin^2(kL/2) = 0.50000. The method of moments gives -709.53 ohm at the feed, within 1.9% of the referred value and nowhere near the unreferred one.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.5-4.6 (eqs. 4-70, 4-79)
Numerically cross-checked against quadrature of the exact pattern integral

archetypes.name: Horizontal dipole over a ground plane
archetypes.summary: Horizontal half-wave dipole at height h above a perfect conductor, solved by image theory with exact mutual impedance.

parameters.name: height above ground
parameters.description: height as a fraction of the free-space wavelength

synthesis.notes: the image sits as far below the plane as the dipole sits above it, with reversed current

analysis.notes: isolated-dipole value, Balanis 4-70

analysis.expr: (eta0/(4*pi))*(2*Ci(k0*d_image) - Ci(k0*(sqrt(d_image**2 + L**2) + L)) - Ci(k0*(sqrt(d_image**2 + L**2) - L)))
analysis.notes: Balanis 8-72a for parallel side-by-side half-wave dipoles. Reproduces the textbook -12.5 ohm at d = lambda/2.

analysis.expr: -(eta0/(4*pi))*(2*Si(k0*d_image) - Si(k0*(sqrt(d_image**2 + L**2) + L)) - Si(k0*(sqrt(d_image**2 + L**2) - L)))
analysis.notes: Balanis 8-72b. Reproduces -29.9 ohm at d = lambda/2.
MINUS, because the image current is reversed. This is why a low horizontal dipole feeds at 30 ohm rather than 73.
field ratio relative to the same current in free space; 2.0 at h = lambda/4
Directivity straight up. Reproduced to five digits by direct numerical integration over the upper hemisphere.
Elevation of the lowest array-factor maximum, where k*h*cos(theta) = pi/2. Pinned at 90 deg (zenith) for h <= lambda/4; 30 deg at h = lambda/2.
the same dipole with no ground present, for comparison

validity: perfectly conducting, infinite ground plane; real earth is lossier and tilts the low-angle lobe
zenith is the pattern peak only for h <= lambda/4 and at h = lambda/4 + n*lambda/2; elsewhere read first_lobe_elevation_deg
mutual impedance formula is the half-wave side-by-side result, so it is exact only near L = lambda/2
no conductor loss: at h = lambda/8 the feed resistance falls to 32 ohm and loss matters more than these figures suggest

known_cases.source: Mutual impedance of parallel half-wave dipoles at d = 0.5 lambda is -12.5 - j29.9 ohm (Balanis 4th ed. Fig. 8.21). Peak directivity independently confirmed at 5.6034 (7.485 dBi) by hemisphere integration.

A dipole one eighth of a wavelength up has HIGHER zenith directivity than one at a quarter wave (8.70 vs 7.48 dBi), because the image adds in phase and the feed resistance collapses to 32 ohm. Confirmed by hemisphere integration.
cos(theta) = lambda/(4h) = 0.5 puts the lobe at 60 deg from zenith, i.e. 30 deg elevation - the standard half-wave-high dipole result

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.7 (image theory) and Ch. 8.6 (eqs. 8-72)
Numerically cross-checked by integrating the full pattern over the upper hemisphere

archetypes.name: Capacitively top-loaded short monopole
archetypes.summary: Electrically short vertical with a top hat that flattens the current taper, raising radiation resistance by up to four times.

parameters.name: top/base current ratio
parameters.description: Top current over base current. DERIVED from the hat now; supply it to override, as before.

parameters.name: number of radial wires in the hat
parameters.description: A solid disc is the many-radial limit and is NOT reached by 32: beta is still rising there.

synthesis.notes: DERIVED FROM THE HAT, which this spec used to say it could not do: its validity read 'relating hat size to beta_top needs a numerical solve this spec does not attempt'. Solved by method of moments on a vertical with a hat of radial wires, over infinite ground by image theory (otahub.num.mom.top_hat_monopole), with junctions joining the radials to the vertical. The base current is read from a straight-line fit to the vertical's current away from the feed, because the delta gap puts a local excess on the feed node of a short wire. Fitted in four dimensionless variables - hat radius over height, height over wire radius, radial count and ELECTRICAL height - over 207 capacitive cases; worst error 0.016 in beta, and 0.027 on held-out cases. The fourth variable was the one first left out, and leaving it out held the error at 0.1 whatever else was tried. Supply beta_top to override.
exact for a linear current taper: the area under the taper divided by the base current

analysis.notes: Rr = 160*pi^2*(h_eff/lambda)^2 for a monopole over a perfect ground plane - half the uniform-current dipole of length 2*h_eff. Collapses to the classic 40*pi^2*(h/lambda)^2 when beta_top = 0. Checked against the solver with the solved beta: the linear-taper formula is within 0.1 to 2.4% of the radiated power across every hat, so the model is sound - it only ever needed the right beta.
the same rod with no hat, for comparison
up to 6.02 dB at beta_top = 1, where the current is fully uniform

Exact for the linear taper: integral of |I/I0|^2 along the rod is h*(1+beta+beta^2)/3, which is h/3 for a bare whip and h when fully loaded. Hat and ground-system loss are NOT included and usually dominate at HF.
exactly 3.0 for any short vertical over an infinite perfect ground plane - twice the free-space dipole's 1.5

Isolated thin DISC, C = 8*eps0*a - a sizing aid for a solid hat. A hat of radials has less, and one close to the ground has more: at 0.02 lambda height a 0.06 lambda hat is three times wider than it is high and behaves more like one plate of a capacitor. beta_top no longer depends on this figure.
Chu/McLean lower bound for a linearly polarised antenna inside a sphere of radius h. No amount of top loading beats this.

validity: h < 0.1*lambda, where the linear current taper is a good description
perfect infinite ground plane; a real radial ground system adds loss resistance that often exceeds Rr

the derived beta_top covers h 0.02 to 0.1 lambda, hat radius 0.005 to 0.06 lambda, 4 to 16 radials and wire radius 1e-6 to 1e-4 lambda, for hats that do NOT resonate the whip by themselves: once the hat is big enough to cancel the reactance the current is no longer a linear taper and the model stops applying
more radials keep raising beta well past 16 - on a 0.01 lambda hat, 0.61 at 16 radials and 0.67 at 32 - so a solid disc does better than any radial count fitted here

input reactance is NOT fitted. No form tried got closer than about 17% on held-out cases, and a short whip is high-Q, so a coil sized from a figure that far off would miss resonance. The solved values are in the tables field
hat and ground loss excluded, so radiation_efficiency is an upper bound

known_cases.source: With no hat the model must return the textbook short-monopole value 40*pi^2*(h/lambda)^2 = 0.987 ohm. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.8
beta_top = 0 is the bare whip, so the loading gain must be exactly 0 dB. Expectations of zero need tol_abs.
A fully uniform current quadruples Rr, exactly 6.02 dB. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., eqs. 4-19 and 4-37
beta = 0.6 gives h_eff/h = 0.8, so Rr = 160*pi^2*0.04^2 = 2.527 ohm. Directivity of any short vertical over perfect ground is 3.0 = 4.771 dBi.

Derived beta for a 0.05 lambda whip with a 0.01 lambda hat of 8 radials, wire radius 3.3e-05 lambda: 0.5207. The nearest solved grid point (a/lambda 0.0001, h 0.05, R 0.01, N 8) gave 0.4965. Rr then follows from the linear-taper formula, which the solver confirms to within 2.4% given the right beta.

Derived beta for a 0.05 lambda whip with a 0.04 lambda hat of 8 radials, wire radius 3.3e-05 lambda: 0.8878. The nearest solved grid point (a/lambda 0.0001, h 0.05, R 0.04, N 8) gave 0.8797. Rr then follows from the linear-taper formula, which the solver confirms to within 2.4% given the right beta.

Derived beta for a 0.03 lambda whip with a 0.02 lambda hat of 16 radials, wire radius 1e-05 lambda: 0.8804. The nearest solved grid point (a/lambda 1e-05, h 0.035, R 0.02, N 16) gave 0.8612. Rr then follows from the linear-taper formula, which the solver confirms to within 2.4% given the right beta.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.8 (monopoles) and eqs. 4-19, 4-37
McLean, A re-examination of the fundamental limits on the radiation Q, IEEE T-AP 44(5), 1996
Top current derived from the hat geometry by method of moments with wire junctions, over infinite ground by image theory

mom_top_hat.source: Method of moments, otahub.num.mom.top_hat_monopole, infinite PEC ground
mom_top_hat.note: The reactance is here rather than in a formula because none fitted well enough to size a coil. Positive reactances are hats big enough to resonate the whip on their own.

archetypes.name: Inductively loaded short monopole
archetypes.summary: Short whip resonated by a series loading coil, with the efficiency penalty the coil brings.

parameters.name: top/base current ratio
parameters.description: 0 for a base-loaded bare whip; centre loading or a hat raises it

parameters.name: loading coil Q
parameters.description: 150-300 for a well-made air-core coil; under 100 for a compact loading inductor

parameters.name: ground system resistance
parameters.description: loss of the radial or vehicle-body ground; 0 for an ideal plane

synthesis.notes: the image makes the monopole behave as a dipole of length 2h, at half the impedance

analysis.notes: Left as the triangular-current result on purpose. The method of moments cannot referee it better than about 10% on a wire this short: its delta gap puts an 8-17% excess on the feed node that grows with mesh refinement, reading R 10% low, while referencing the power to the smooth current instead reads 6% high. The closed form sits inside that bracket and agrees with the sinusoidal-current input resistance to 1.3%.

Half the dipole's FEED-POINT reactance, because a monopole on an infinite ground plane sees half the dipole's impedance. Balanis 4-79 is referred to the current MAXIMUM of the assumed sinusoid; for any length but lambda/2 that point is not the feed, and the feed-point value is the current-maximum one divided by sin^2(kL/2) - the same referral this catalogue already applied to the resistance. This spec used the current-maximum value, which for a short whip is catastrophic: at h = 0.05 lambda sin^2(kL/2) = 0.0955, so the reactance, the loading inductance and the coil loss were all about ten times too small. A 1.5 m whip at 10 MHz shows about -j1163 ohm, not -j111. Independently: the method of moments and Hallen's equation both land within 4% of the corrected value, and Schelkunoff's transmission-line model, cruder, within 20%.

series inductance that cancels the antenna reactance at f0. Was about ten times too small before the feed referral: a coil wound to the old figure leaves the whip still strongly capacitive, a hundred half-bandwidths from resonance at h = 0.05 lambda.

R = |X|/Q. This is the dominant loss in most loaded whips, and it grows as the antenna shortens - exactly where Rr is collapsing. With the reactance referred correctly it is about SIX times the radiation resistance for a 0.05 lambda whip and a Q-200 coil, not 'over half' as this spec used to say.
what the transmitter sees at resonance. A convenient 50 ohm here is usually bad news: it means loss, not radiation.

validity: h < 0.1*lambda
single lumped coil, assumed lossless apart from its Q; distributed loading behaves better
coil placement is captured only through beta_top, not modelled directly
ground loss is an input, and at HF it commonly exceeds every other term

known_cases.source: A 1.5 m whip at 10 MHz: Rr = 0.9870 ohm from the short-monopole formula, and X = -1162.7 ohm from Balanis 4-79 halved AND referred to the feed by sin^2(kL/2) = 0.09549. The method of moments gives -1140.2 ohm by image theory, within 2.0%. This case used to assert -111.03 ohm, the current-maximum value - ten times too small.

L = |X|/omega = 1162.7/(2*pi*10e6) = 18.51 uH, and R_coil = |X|/Q = 5.814 ohm - 5.9 times the radiation resistance. This case used to give 1.77 uH and 0.555 ohm, 'over half the radiation resistance'; a coil wound to that figure leaves the whip still strongly capacitive.

Rr/(Rr + R_coil + R_rod) = 0.9870/(0.9870 + 5.8136 + 0.0656) = 0.1437, i.e. -8.4 dB. With the reactance at its old current-maximum value the same sum gave 0.6139 (-2.1 dB): the old spec overstated a short loaded whip's efficiency by a factor of 4.3.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.5-4.8 (eq. 4-79)
ARRL Antenna Book, mobile and shortened-vertical chapters, for the coil-Q and ground-loss ranges

archetypes.name: Turnstile (crossed dipoles in quadrature)
archetypes.summary: Two crossed half-wave dipoles fed 90 degrees apart: circular polarisation on axis, near-omnidirectional in the plane of the elements.

synthesis.notes: tip-to-tip, each element

A quarter-wave of line in one feed is the classic way to get the 90 degrees. It is narrowband - the axial ratio degrades either side of f0 - and the line's electrical length must account for its own velocity factor.

analysis.notes: one element in isolation; the crossed elements barely couple
Equal to a SINGLE dipole's directivity. Splitting the power two ways is exactly offset by the two orthogonal polarisations adding on axis - confirmed by numerical integration.
Along either element axis, where only the other dipole radiates: exactly 3 dB below the axial value, about -0.86 dBi for half-wave elements.
The 45-degree azimuth, where the pattern dips. Powers add because the two polarisations are orthogonal, so there is no interference term.
About 1.03 dB for exactly half-wave elements - the turnstile is near-omnidirectional but not perfectly so
perfect circular polarisation on axis, by symmetry, when the feed is exactly in quadrature

each element behaves essentially as an isolated dipole. Now referred to the FEED - both parts divided by sin^2(kL/2). At the default 0.4788 lambda that moves the impedance by only 0.45%, but it was the same omission as its neighbours and would not have stayed small at any other length.

validity: mutual coupling between the crossed elements is neglected; it is genuinely small because each sits in the other's null
exact quadrature assumed - the quarter-wave line achieves it at one frequency only
free space, no reflector; a turnstile over a ground plane or with a crossed reflector behaves quite differently
circular polarisation holds only on the axis normal to both elements; the element plane is linearly polarised

known_cases.source: Numerical integration over the full sphere of U = |Fx|^2 + |Fy|^2 gives D = 1.64092 on axis and 0.82046 along an element - identical to a single dipole on axis, exactly 3 dB down in the element plane.
The 45-degree azimuth minimum is 0.64702 (-1.891 dBi), giving 1.03 dB of ripple. Independently reproduced on a 1201 x 2402 angular grid.
symmetry: equal-amplitude orthogonal fields in exact quadrature are circular by construction

references: Brown, The turnstile antenna, Electronics 9, 1936
Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.6 for the element, Ch. 6 for polarisation
Numerically cross-checked by spherical integration of the summed-power pattern
